shadows.name: board-paint
shadows.purpose: Not elevation: paints the board colour out to the screen edges behind the board header, clipped to the top.

shadows.name: lit-filter

motion.name: step
motion.purpose: Every level change: board colour, header turn (from translateX(-10px)), active tab run-out (clip-path from inset(0 45% 0 0)), front-page tab nudge. Removed entirely under reduced motion.

narrative.overview:
StudyTrack is a boxed-software reference manual with acetate leaves over coloured tab boards. Every Cambridge level is a divider in a ring binder, and the screen's whole ground is the current level's board at full strength, so a student or the teacher knows which class they are in from the colour of the screen before reading a word. The work sits on one milky, near-white leaf laid over the board, always in the same place. The dashboard and My progress are the binder's graphite cover, and so are the front page and the sign-in screen: the binder seen from outside, with the level tabs stepping down its fore edge.

The world is flat and printed. Boards are solid colour; nothing is graded, glossed or lifted. Depth comes only from stacking: board, then leaf, then the rules drawn on the leaf. Inside a leaf, work is ruled rather than boxed, the way a manual sets a section: a heavy rule opens it and hairlines divide its rows. One grotesque, Archivo, does all the reading, condensed and heavy on its width axis for heads the way a tab's label is set; Red Hat Mono is kept for what is genuinely code or a figure. Changes do not ease: a divider is turned, in two frames over 90 ms.

The system refuses the category default of one grey ground, one accent and the same white cards on every screen whatever the subject.
keyCharacteristics: The current level's board fills the screen ground; the work sits on a single leaf above it.
The active sidebar entry is a tab that runs out across the rail and joins the board.
Flat boards: no gradients, no decorative shadows.
Sections on a leaf are ruled, not carded.
Archivo on its width axis for everything; Red Hat Mono only for syllabus codes, marks and counts.
Two-frame stepped motion (90 ms, `steps(2, end)`); reduced motion swaps instantly.

rules.name: The Whole Ground Rule
rules.body: The current level's board is the screen's ground at full strength, set once by `data-level` on the shell. Components read `--board`, `--on-board`, `--level` and `--on-level`; they never pick a level hue by hand, except a tab that names its own level.

rules.name: The Board and Leaf Rule
rules.body: The board colour is for large ground and tabs; on the leaf, a level speaks only through its reading colour (`--level`). Never set leaf text in a board hue.

rules.name: The Errata Rule
rules.body: Vermilion is reserved for errors. A waiting count, a deadline or a highlight is never vermilion; on the cover, the queue figure is in the cover's ink and turns the classroom's lit green (`#8dd068`) when nothing waits.

rules.name: The One Grotesque Rule
rules.body: Archivo does all the reading and interface; heads get their character from the width axis (78 to 88%) and weight (750 to 800), never from a third family.

rules.name: The Context In The Heading Rule
rules.body: What a label above a heading would say travels inside the heading: the syllabus code is set large in the mono beside the level name ("Stage 7 mastery 0862", mono at weight 400), and a quieter aside (the tier, "practice complete") follows on the leaf at 0.62em in muted Archivo after a middle dot. The only line above a heading is the board's running head (below).

rules.name: The Figures Are Mono Rule
rules.body: Scores, counts, marks and syllabus codes are set in Red Hat Mono with tabular numerals; prose numbers are not.

rules.name: The Flat Boards Rule
rules.body: No gradients and no decorative shadows anywhere: boards, leaves, panels, buttons and Clerk's sign-in card are all shadowless.

rules.name: The Ruled Not Boxed Rule
rules.body: A section on a leaf opens with a 2px ink rule and divides its rows with 1px hairlines; it has no background, border box or radius. The one lit section, this week's focus, opens with a 4px rule in the level colour instead.

rules.name: The Running Head Rule
rules.body: The line above the board heading is a reference manual's running head: the real syllabus and section ("Cambridge Lower Secondary Mathematics"), once per screen, only on the board, ruled off. It never carries an invented label, and no other heading on any surface gets a label above it.

rules.name: The Two Frame Rule
rules.body: Every change of level steps, it does not ease: `90ms steps(2, end)` for the board colour, the header turn, the tab run-out and the front-page tab nudge. Under reduced motion, all of it swaps instantly.

dos: **Do** set `data-level` on the shell and let every component read `--board`, `--on-board`, `--level` and `--on-level`.
**Do** put the screen's heading on the board and the work on one leaf below it.
**Do** open sections on a leaf with a 2px ink rule and divide rows with hairlines.
**Do** set syllabus codes, marks and counts in Red Hat Mono with tabular numerals, and put the code inside the heading.
**Do** keep corners at 4px (2px for error slips, 0 for ruled sections).
**Do** animate level changes with `90ms steps(2, end)` and drop them entirely under reduced motion.
**Do** keep drawing and writing surfaces that frame a printed page white in every theme.
donts: **Don't** use vermilion for anything but errors.
**Don't** use gradients or decorative shadows; boards and leaves are flat.
**Don't** box a leaf's sections as cards or a card grid, or fill a section with a tinted background.
**Don't** set leaf text in a board hue; use the level's reading colour.
**Don't** put a small-capitals label or eyebrow above a heading; the board's running head is the only line above a heading.
**Don't** ease level changes or fade them; a divider is turned.
**Don't** add a third type family or use glyphs from text faces as icons; the portal has one 24px stroke icon set.
